Updated runs from the China Meteorological Administration and ECMWF later today will be the next key data points for traders.

eventMetadata.context_description: Recent PAGASA forecasts for Metro Manila on June 1 project a daily maximum near 30°C amid 60% rain chances and partly cloudy conditions, anchoring trader sentiment around 31–33°C outcomes that together exceed 75% implied probability. This positioning reflects the transition toward ENSO-neutral conditions after La Niña, with models indicating warmer-than-average surface temperatures for the region and typical early southwest monsoon influences that moderate extremes through increased cloud cover and showers. Historical June averages near 32°C provide baseline context, while short-range model variability in steering patterns and localized convection creates the observed spread; upcoming updated PAGASA briefings and numerical weather prediction runs will likely refine these probabilities ahead of resolution.
